rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are grounded in historical metrics from reference project 004-healthcare-patient-app (Patient Appointment and Telehealth App, 3,900 total hours, 22 weeks). Key modules such as the Flutter mobile app (820-950h vs 900h ref), scheduling engine (480-540h vs 520h ref), Twilio/WebRTC video consultation (350-410h vs 380h ref), secure messaging and reminders (390-440h vs 420h ref), counsellor web dashboard (520-600h vs 560h ref), HIPAA compliance (280-330h vs 300h ref), and QA/Store release (320-380h vs 340h ref) directly match historical baselines. The external EHR/HL7 FHIR integration module (480h) present in the reference was excluded as this startup relies on an internal client records model rather than external hospital systems; DevOps and cloud infrastructure work (240-290h) was explicitly delineated to reflect production containerized deployment requirements.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 007-edtech-lms (Learning Management System for Corporate Training, 2,800 total hours, 18 weeks duration), which featured identical core architectural requirements including video tracking (300h), assessment attempt engines (340h), certification rules (360h), SCORM import/player (420h), reporting (280h), user management (220h), and DevOps/QA (400h). Scope has been tuned specifically to plant supervisor hierarchies and factory floor operational conditions, yielding an aligned estimate range of 2,490 to 2,940 engineering hours across an 18-week delivery timeframe.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical reference project data from 'Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians' (id=008-mobile-field-service, total delivery effort 3,600 hours over 21 weeks). Scope elements closely mirror that reference: offline synchronization and conflict resolution (720-800h vs 760h ref), mobile job list/checklists (480-560h vs 520h ref), photo/signature capture and upload queues (280-330h vs 300h ref), back-office scheduling console (600-680h vs 640h ref), ERP work order and invoice synchronization (490-560h vs 520h ref), background services and push notifications (180-220h vs 200h ref), DevOps and store deployment (240-280h vs 260h ref), and QA with field pilot testing (380-430h vs 400h ref). Lessons learned regarding conflict resolution complexity and device fragmentation were incorporated by allocating full dedicated effort to testing and sync isolation.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from Reference Project 001-logistics-fleet-portal (3,000 total hours, 20 weeks). In the benchmark project, telematics integration for 3 vendors required 520h; here, integrating 2 telematics vendors is scoped at 360-440h, preserving necessary buffer for protocol discrepancies learned from the reference. The live map module is scaled from 420h down slightly to 380-450h due to tracking 250 buses instead of 600+. Route deviation and idle alert hours are adapted from the reference's 380h engine to 340-420h to incorporate specific school bus corridor checks. Daily route reporting matches the 360h benchmark allocation at 300-380h. DevOps (180-230h) and QA/UAT (520-640h) account for rigorous end-to-end field simulation and vendor payload variability based on reference project lessons.

Estimates are strictly modeled on historical data from reference project '003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace' (6,100 hours, 30 weeks). Directly analogous modules were aligned to that baseline: the dealer inventory import pipeline (520-640h vs reference 620h), faceted search engine (440-540h vs reference 540h), Stripe Connect marketplace split payouts (600-720h vs reference 700h), dealer portal (580-700h vs reference 820h), admin back-office (420-520h vs reference 520h), SSR frontend (320-380h vs reference 340h), DevOps/load testing (360-420h vs reference 380h), and QA/UAT (780-940h vs reference 920h). Non-applicable B2B features (customer-specific pricing at 780h and punch-out integration at 480h) were removed. In their place, custom modules with no direct reference analogue were added bottom-up: the core real-time bidding engine with anti-sniping and Redis lock coordination (680-820h) and the dedicated buyer account/bidding dashboard (360-440h), resulting in a realistic delivery profile of 5,060 to 6,120 total engineering hours across 26 weeks.

Estimates were synthesized using two direct reference projects: '002-fintech-kyc-onboarding' (5,200h, 26 weeks) and '003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace' (6,100h, 30 weeks). The worker verification modules, document encryption, and compliance review console are directly derived from Project 002's KYC wizard (480h), vendor integrations (460h IDV + 340h PEP/sanctions), review console (720h), and PII security (420h). The shift marketplace, search/filtering, and payment flows map to Project 003's search/faceted filtering (540h), Stripe Connect integration (700h), supplier portal (820h), and admin moderation (520h). Scope adjustments were made: we reduced the catalogue import and punch-out components from 003, while incorporating shift-specific concurrency controls and attendance tracking. DevOps and QA allocations (approx. 1,400h to 1,650h combined) match historical delivery norms for multi-stakeholder fintech and marketplace platforms requiring strict regulatory compliance.

Estimates are derived directly from Reference Project 006 (Embedded Analytics Dashboard, 4,600 hours) and Reference Project 001 (Fleet Tracking Portal, 3,000 hours). The analytical foundation closely matches Project 006: event ingestion via Kafka (estimated at 460-540h vs 520h reference), ClickHouse modeling (520-620h vs 640h reference), tenant query API (420-500h vs 560h reference), customizable drag-and-drop dashboards (780-920h vs 1,000h reference, adjusted downward slightly for a more constrained widget library), and scheduled reports/PDF export (300-360h vs 380h reference). The multi-tenant organization and RBAC model is adopted directly from Project 001 (160-200h vs 160h reference). For the modules without direct equivalents in Project 006, the alert engine is benchmarked against Project 001's route deviation and alerts engine (340-420h vs 380h reference), and the installer device configuration portal is aligned with Project 001's asset management CRUD (240-300h vs 240h reference). QA, DevOps, and performance testing hours have been scaled to reflect total end-to-end integration and load testing required across the combined streaming and analytics architecture.

The estimates are synthesized directly from historical reference projects: (1) Reference 008 (Offline-First Field Service App, 3600h total) informed the offline SQLite data layer, sync engine, background sync, mobile testing, and QA field pilot efforts. Offline data layer hours were benchmarked against Reference 008's sync (760h) and adjusted to 520-680h given that doctor visit logs represent a more bounded conflict model than technician parts/dispatch. The Salesforce CRM integration (380-480h) was modeled on Reference 008's ERP integration (520h). (2) Reference 005 (Internal HR Knowledge Assistant RAG, 1500h total) informed the AI ingestion, chunking, embeddings (220-280h vs 240h ref), hybrid retrieval and citations (180-240h vs 200h ref), and evaluation/compliance benchmarking (140-180h vs 160h ref). Adjustments were made to incorporate strict page-level citation requirements and mobile-optimized PDF rendering.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 004-healthcare-patient-app (total: 3,900 hours, 22 weeks), which implemented a similar Flutter mobile app, FastAPI backend, scheduling engine, video integration, and administrative portal. Key modules like Scheduling (460-540h vs 520h reference) and Video Consultations (350-420h vs 380h reference) closely match the historical telemetry. The legacy EHR/FHIR integration (480h) from the reference project has been replaced with the Wearables Integration (440-520h) and Challenge/Leaderboard Engine (280-350h). An additional 2 weeks and corresponding hours were allocated to account for multi-tenant HR enterprise reporting, Redis leaderboard aggregation, and the stringent store compliance requirements for Google Health Connect.

Estimates are grounded in historical metrics from reference project 003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace (Angular, Node.js, Azure). Specifically, the external inventory sync module (280-360h) adapts the baseline catalogue import pipeline (620h) adjusted downward for a focused distributor integration. The manager review portal (220-280h) is informed by the reference admin back-office module (520h). Modules unique to this scope (PWA barcode ingestion, shelf discrepancy engine, and automated PO proposal generation) were estimated bottom-up. DevOps (160-220h) and QA (260-340h) reflect proportional adjustments from reference project hours (380h DevOps and 920h QA) scaled to match this platform's focused feature footprint.

No reference projects were provided for this proposal. The estimates have been constructed bottom-up based on general software engineering delivery experience for production-grade cross-platform mobile apps. Hours reflect complete human lifecycle effort including discovery, UI/UX design, full-stack development, offline data synchronisation, QA/UAT, CI/CD, and post-launch stabilisation. Given the absence of historical reference baselines, a standard variance buffer between minimum and maximum hours is maintained to account for requirements elaboration.

Estimates are grounded in historical data from Reference Project 008-mobile-field-service (Field Service App, 3,600 total hours). In that benchmark, the 'Scheduling and dispatch web console' required 640 hours. For this medical rota solution, that core scheduling domain was adapted into discrete web modules: Manager Shift Definition (140-180h), Automated Rota Generation (170-230h), and the Rule Violation Checker (130-175h). Conversely, substantial non-applicable mobile modules from Project 008—such as offline SQLite data sync (760h), hardware capture (300h), and ERP integrations (520h)—were omitted entirely since the client requested a responsive web tool without third-party integrations. DevOps (90-125h vs 260h in ref) and QA/UAT (120-160h vs 400h in ref) were scaled proportionally to account for web-only browser validation and constraint solver correctness testing for a 30-person staff roster.

No historical reference projects were provided in the prompt. Estimates were developed bottom-up based on standard engineering lifecycles for multi-tier enterprise web applications. Scope estimates factor in discovery, UI/UX design, full-stack implementation, financial-grade ledger validation, third-party vendor integration, automated CI/CD, comprehensive QA/UAT, and post-launch stabilisation.

Because no prior reference projects were provided, this estimate is derived bottom-up using enterprise delivery baselines. Hours account for full lifecycle activities including architecture, UX design, cross-browser touch/stylus support, real-time WebSocket protocol resilience, comprehensive QA under synthetic multi-user loads, and production cloud infrastructure.
